overview.summary: New Zealand early childhood education and care includes teacher-led education and care centres, kindergartens, home-based services, playcentres, kōhanga reo and hospital-based services. Private operators generally combine Ministry funding with parent fees. Economics depend on licensed capacity, attendance, funded child hours, age mix, fee collection, qualified staffing, ratios, property cost and consistent regulatory quality. A centre's local catchment and reputation are more relevant than national participation alone.
business_models: Centre-based education and care charging parent fees and receiving government funding
Kindergarten or community-led services with different governance and funding characteristics
Home-based networks coordinating educators and families under a licensed service
Multi-site private groups sharing management, curriculum, systems and marketing
Property-owning or related-party property structures separated from the operating service
industry_structure: Single-centre and regional owners coexist with larger groups and community-based providers.
Services compete within local catchments on trust, quality, hours, philosophy, convenience, fees and reputation.
Licensing, funding, staffing and premises requirements limit capacity and shape operating leverage.
demand_drivers: Local population of children by age, household employment and commuting patterns
Participation, funded hours, affordability and government funding settings
Service reputation, education philosophy, opening hours and location
Housing development, competing licensed capacity and family movement
margin_and_cost_drivers: Occupancy or attendance by age and day, funded hours and parent-fee yield
Qualified teacher mix, ratios, roster efficiency, relief staff and wage rates
Rent, rates, food, resources, insurance and premises maintenance
Funding accuracy, fee arrears, compliance, professional development and administration
cyclicality_and_seasonality: Demand is relatively recurring but affected by births, local demographics, school transitions and family employment.
Attendance varies through school holidays, illness periods and annual age transitions.
A local oversupply of licensed places can create sustained occupancy and fee pressure.
overview.working_capital_profile: Government funding and parent-fee timing can produce a relatively recurring receipt profile, while wages are the dominant frequent cost. Funding adjustments, fee arrears, subsidies, holiday staffing and tax obligations require reconciliation. Enrolment or licensed capacity should not be substituted for actual attendance and billable or funded hours.
overview.asset_intensity: Centre operations require suitable licensed premises, fit-out, outdoor areas, furniture, learning equipment and maintenance. Property may be leased, owned in the operating entity or held by a related party. Leasehold fit-out has limited alternative-use value; freehold property needs a separate appraisal and market rent.
regulatory_and_compliance: Education and Training Act, Early Childhood Services Regulations and current licensing criteria
Qualified staff, person-responsible, ratio, first-aid and police-vetting requirements
Curriculum, health and safety, premises, governance, child-protection and record obligations
Funding Handbook, attendance and enrolment records, financial reporting and audit requirements where applicable

subsectors.name: Private centre-based education and care
subsectors.business_model: Licensed centre places generate government funding and parent fees based on attendance, hours and age mix.
subsectors.working_capital: Funding and fees recur, but arrears, funding wash-ups and payroll need tight controls.
subsectors.asset_intensity: Premises and fit-out intensive, with property structure central.

subsectors.name: Home-based early learning
subsectors.business_model: A licensed service coordinates educators providing care in homes with qualified oversight.
subsectors.working_capital: Funding and parent receipts must be matched to educator payments and accurate attendance.
subsectors.asset_intensity: Lower premises intensity but higher network, supervision and educator-continuity dependence.

subsectors.name: Kindergarten and community-led services
subsectors.business_model: Community or association governance combines public funding, fees where applicable and mission-led delivery.
subsectors.working_capital: Funding is central; reserves and restricted funds require interpretation.
subsectors.asset_intensity: Premises may be owned, leased or community-provided.
valuation_watchpoints: Commercial valuation may be inappropriate or constrained

subsectors.name: Multi-site early learning group
subsectors.business_model: Multiple licensed centres share central management, curriculum, finance, recruitment and marketing.
subsectors.working_capital: Group cash can conceal weak centres; funding, tax and payroll should be reconciled by site.
subsectors.asset_intensity: Multiple leases or properties and centre fit-outs create portfolio obligations.

primary_risks.mechanism: Lower attendance or new competing places reduces funding and fees while staffing and property costs remain.
Qualified-staff shortages or absence can increase relief cost, constrain licensed operation or create compliance risk.
Licence conditions, poor records or funding errors can reduce receipts, require repayment or interrupt service.
Loss of premises, onerous rent or one underperforming centre can impair the business.

cash_conversion_and_working_capital: Reconcile licensed capacity, enrolment, attendance, funded hours and parent billing.
Review funding wash-ups, fee arrears, subsidies and holiday attendance.
Confirm payroll, PAYE, holiday pay and relief staffing are fully recorded.
Model occupancy at daily and age-group level through the school transition cycle.
collateral_considerations: Leasehold fit-out and learning equipment usually have limited recovery.
Freehold premises require an independent valuation and market-rent separation.
Funding receivables depend on compliant records and may be subject to adjustment.
Licence, goodwill, families and staff are operating assets rather than reliable standalone collateral.
downside_stresses: Occupancy fall with only partial staff reduction
Lease renewal at higher rent plus maintenance spend
monitoring_kpis: Occupancy and attendance by centre, day and age
Qualified staffing, ratios, turnover and relief cost
Wages and rent as percentages of revenue
Cash, DSCR, tax and funding adjustments
covenant_considerations: Restrictions on distributions while tax, funding or licence issues exist
Prompt notice of licence conditions, material review findings, centre closure or key lease event
diligence_questions: What are licensed places, actual attendance and break-even occupancy by centre, day and age?
How do government funding and parent fees reconcile to attendance records?
Are qualification, person-responsible, ratio, first-aid and police-vetting requirements consistently met?
What are staff turnover, relief usage, wage commitments and recruitment needs?
Are premises suitable, leases transferable and maintenance funded over the debt term?

value_drivers: Stable occupancy supported by local catchment and reputation
Qualified, stable leadership and teaching team
Transferable suitable premises and clean licensing history
Scalable multi-site systems with transparent site economics
multiple_influences: Mature centres with stable occupancy and management depth are more predictable than ramp-up or owner-dependent sites.
Property ownership must be separated through market rent and an independent appraisal.
Licence issues, staff shortages, local oversupply and short leases reduce value.
normalisation_focus: Normal occupancy rather than a short peak or ramp-up period
Market owner-manager and pedagogical leadership remuneration
Compliant wage, relief and holiday-pay cost
Market rent and ongoing premises maintenance
Funding adjustments and one-off opening costs
peer_selection: Match centre-based, home-based and multi-site models.
Compare age mix, occupancy, local market, property structure, funding, staffing and maturity.
Do not treat community or restricted providers as ordinary commercial peers without adjustment.
preferred_metrics: EV/EBITDA after market rent and management remuneration
EV per licensed place only as a secondary check after occupancy, quality and location alignment
DCF for ramp-up or changing funding and lease economics
Free cash flow after premises maintenance
discount_and_premium_factors: Premium indicators include stable mature occupancy, strong reputation, clean compliance, staff depth and good tenure.
Discount indicators include local oversupply, licence conditions, wage pressure, staff dependence, short lease and funding-record issues.
diligence_questions: What occupancy and fee yield are maintainable after school transitions and local competition?
What staff and rent costs are required on a standalone basis?
Will licence, premises, families and key staff remain through a change of control?
How should freehold or related-party property be separated from operating value?

market_research_sections.credit_paper:
Early childhood education and care combines recurring family demand with government funding and a detailed licensing and staffing framework. Education Counts publishes participation, service and staffing data that can frame national and regional conditions, while Ministry of Education guidance defines current licensing, qualified-staff and person-responsible requirements. These sources do not establish a centre's local demand, quality or compliance; credit analysis must use centre-level attendance, staffing, funding and property evidence.

Licensed capacity is not revenue. The lender should reconcile places, enrolment, actual attendance, funded child hours, age mix and parent billing by day and centre. Wages and property are major semi-fixed costs, so lower occupancy, relief staffing or wage pressure can reduce coverage quickly. Funding adjustments, fee arrears, payroll, holiday pay and tax should be tested. Leasehold fit-out provides limited recovery, while freehold property requires a separate appraisal and market rent.

Licence status, review findings, accurate attendance records, qualified staffing, ratios, child protection and suitable premises are continuity risks as well as compliance matters. The paper should assess break-even occupancy, local competing capacity, staff retention, lease tenure and maintenance. For groups, weak sites should not be hidden by consolidated averages. Covenants and conditions should focus on liquidity, licence events, funding adjustments and transparent centre-level reporting.
market_research_sections.valuation_report:
An early learning service's value is determined primarily by maintainable attendance and fee yield within its local catchment, delivered by a stable qualified team in suitable, transferable premises with clean licensing and funding records. Education Counts participation data provides useful national and regional context, but valuation requires centre-level occupancy by day and age, local competing capacity, waitlists, staff ratios, fees, funding and reputation.

Normalised earnings should use sustainable rather than peak or short ramp-up occupancy, replacement remuneration for owner-management and pedagogical roles, compliant wages and relief cover, market rent and normal premises maintenance. Government funding and parent fees must reconcile to attendance. Freehold or related-party property should be separately appraised and charged a market rent; leasehold fit-out should not be assumed to recover at book value.

Transferable value is stronger where occupancy is mature and diversified across cohorts, the licence and review history are clean, staffing is stable, systems are documented, and the lease or property position supports continuity. Local oversupply, licence conditions, funding-record issues, teacher shortages, short tenure and owner or centre-manager dependence reduce forecast confidence. EV per licensed place can only be a secondary cross-check after these differences are reconciled; this pack does not provide a current sector multiple.

limitations: National participation does not establish demand or occupancy in the subject centre's catchment.
Funding settings, licensing criteria and staff requirements are time-sensitive and must be checked at the report date.
Attendance, funding, staffing, licence, review, lease and property evidence must be obtained for the subject service.
No property value, fit-out recovery value, EV per place or current transaction multiple is supplied.
